annualFullTime.source: Fair Work Commission Annual Wage Review 2026, reported by ABC: national minimum wage A$26.44/h and A$1,004.90/week (38-hour week) from 1 Jul 2026, up 5.97% from A$24.95/A$948. https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-06-02/minimum-wage-increase-june-2026-australia/106746542 (the FWC decision PDF and the DEWR ministerial release appeared in search results but were not opened)

minimumWage.arithmetic: A$1,004.90 per week x 52 weeks = A$52,254.80 (A$26.44 x 38 h = A$1,004.72; FWC publishes A$1,004.90). Excludes 12% employer super. Casual workers get a 25% loading on top (A$33.05/h).

drivingAge.source: State road authorities (for example Transport for NSW, VicRoads). drivingAge.note: Learner at 16 (ACT 15y9m) needs a supervising driver. A provisional P1 licence lets you drive alone from 17 in most states, with limits on passengers, speed and alcohol. Victoria's first solo (probationary) licence is at 18. Fully unrestricted licences come later, around 20 or 21.

livingCost.basis: Single adult in a typical mid-sized capital. Net need about A$46.6k: 1-bed rent outside the city centre A$1,774 a month (A$21.3k a year) plus A$1,600 a month for food, utilities, phone, internet and a transport pass (A$19.2k a year) gives A$40.5k, plus about 15% for health cover and clothing. Gross A$55,000 leaves about A$46.6k after 2025-26 resident income tax (A$8,388 including 2% Medicare levy). This is just above the A$52,255 minimum wage.

tuition.notes: Commonwealth-supported fees are set nationally by discipline band, not by university, so the community/state/elite tiers for bachelor, medicine and law are mapped to bands rather than institutions. The 2026 bands per 1.0 EFTSL (48 units) are A$4,738 (education, nursing, languages, English, clinical psychology), A$9,537 (science, engineering, computing, allied health), A$13,558 (medicine, dentistry, veterinary) and A$17,399 (law, accounting, administration, economics, commerce, communications, society and culture). Students who started before 2021 pay lower grandfathered rates. HECS-HELP lets students defer the whole amount. Master, vocational and TAFE figures are estimates.

Taken from secondary sites because the ATO page returned 403 and the Department of Education page timed out. https://fairworkmate.com.au/blog/hecs-indexation-june-2026-australia ; also listed in search: https://atotaxcalculator.com.au/hecs-debt-indexation

studentLoan.description: HELP (HECS-HELP) is interest-free but indexed every 1 June to the lower of CPI and the Wage Price Index (2.8% in June 2026). Rates in this entry are percentages. Real rate is about -1.2% (2.8 minus 4.0 inflation). Repayment is income-contingent through the tax system, starting at about A$69,528 of income in 2026-27 (secondary source). A one-off 20% cut to HELP debts was applied in 2025 (from my recollection, not verified in this run).

schooling.primarySchool: Primary school (Foundation, Prep or Kindergarten to Year 6). Compulsory schooling starts at about age 5 to 6, depending on the state.
schooling.middleSchool: Junior secondary or high school, Years 7 to 10 (ages about 12 to 16). Year 7 is in secondary school in every state, including Queensland since 2015 and South Australia since 2022.
schooling.schoolLeaving: Senior secondary certificate in Years 11 and 12, awarded by each state: HSC (NSW), VCE (Victoria), QCE (Queensland), SACE (South Australia), WACE (Western Australia), TCE (Tasmania), ACT Senior Secondary Certificate. Students needing a university place receive an ATAR.
schooling.vocational: TAFE (Technical and Further Education) and other registered training organisations: Certificates I to IV, Diplomas, and apprenticeships or traineeships. VET subjects can also be taken inside Years 11 to 12.
schooling.tierCommunity: TAFE and other vocational colleges, and regional or dual-sector institutions (TAFE NSW, Victoria University, regional campuses)
schooling.tierState: Mainstream public universities (for example Deakin, University of Newcastle, Griffith)
schooling.tierElite: Group of Eight research universities (Melbourne, Sydney, ANU, UNSW, Monash, Queensland, Adelaide, Western Australia)
schooling.gradeSystem: ATAR runs from 0.00 to 99.95 in steps of 0.05 (there is no 100). It is a percentile rank against the whole age group, not a mark, so an ATAR of 80 means the top 20%. Higher is better and there is no pass mark. The usual average is about 70; the top possible result is 99.95. NSW and ACT report anything below 30 as '30 or less'. Every state produces comparable ATARs. Competitive courses such as medicine or top law often ask for 95 to 99+ (my recollection).
schooling.startingAges: Compulsory schooling starts at 5 to 6 with Foundation or Prep. Primary runs to about age 12 (Year 6). Lower secondary is Years 7 to 10 (about 12 to 16). Upper secondary is Years 11 to 12 (about 16 to 18). Most states require schooling or training until 16 or 17. There is no early track split; vocational options sit alongside academic ones.

highlights: Australia has a national minimum wage of A$26.44 an hour, about A$52,000 a year full-time, and the typical full-time worker earns about A$98,000.
University fees are set by subject, A$4,738 to A$17,399 a year, and HECS-HELP loans carry no interest but are indexed yearly (2.8% in June 2026, below 4.0% inflation).
caveats: The session's WebSearch budget ran out after four searches, so most of this was gathered with WebFetch and my own knowledge. Verified to a primary or reputable page: minimum wage (ABC reporting the Fair Work Commission ruling), ABS median full-time earnings (May 2025), ABS CPI (4.0% to Aug 2026), RBA exchange rate, World Bank PPP, the 2026 student-contribution bands (two university pages) and the ATAR definition (UAC). The ATO, Department of Education, Job Outlook, NSW Police and most state pay pages returned 403, 404, DNS errors or timeouts. The HECS indexation of 2.8% rests on secondary sites. Every occupation pay figure except the ABS medians is a low-confidence estimate. Indeed and SEEK figures mix levels, casual loading and sometimes 40-hour assumptions, so I anchored on award-style logic and my recollection of Job Outlook medians, rounded. The P90 is an estimate scaled from ABS all-employee data. Vocational, master and CEO figures, the specialist and pilot scales, and the driving age were not sourced this run. Figures are gross and exclude the 12% employer super. Annualising uses 52 weeks and a 38-hour week. The 2026 minimum wage applies from 1 July 2026; pay figures for other jobs are roughly 2025-26 levels unless noted.
